Mitigation proposal: Establish a closed-loop “screw-recovery/weight drift” control using only existing sensors (barrel thermocouples, cycle-time logger, and check-weigher).

DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: The driving variables are the check-weigher output ($W$) and the cycle-time logger’s screw recovery time ($t_{rec}$). An increase in part weight ($W$) above target indicates insufficient material density or volume, which is driven by an increase in screw recovery time ($t_{rec}$). The corrective mechanism operates in the following direction: as $t_{rec}$ increases, the system must increase the back-off speed ($v_{backoff}$) to reduce recovery time and ensure more complete metering; as $W$ remains high or variability persists, the system increases the injection hold pressure ($P_{hold}$) to stabilize melt density. Therefore, the direction of effect is: Higher $t_{rec}$ $ightarrow$ Higher $v_{backoff}$; Higher $W$ (or persistent deviation) $ightarrow$ Higher $P_{hold}$. This reduces $t_{rec}$ and brings $W$ back to target while keeping barrel temperature setpoints unchanged.

Implementation:
1) From the check-weigher, compute rolling average part weight ($W_{avg}$) and deviation from target ($\Delta W = W_{avg} - W_{target}$).
2) From the cycle-time logger, compute rolling average screw recovery time ($t_{rec,avg}$) and detect increases beyond a baseline threshold.
3) When both conditions persist for a defined window, trigger a corrective action: increase the back-off speed ($v_{backoff}$) to ensure more complete metering and/or increase injection hold pressure ($P_{hold}$) slightly to stabilize density, while keeping barrel temperature setpoints unchanged.
4) Log the adjustments and verify with subsequent check-weigher readings that weight returns to target and recovery time stabilizes.

Measures relied on: Existing sensors only—barrel thermocouples (to confirm no temperature drift is causing the issue, using existing temperature readings $T_{zone}$), cycle-time logger (for recovery time monitoring, using existing time-stamps $t_{cycle}$ and $t_{phase}$ to derive $t_{rec}$), and check-weigher (for part weight feedback, using existing mass readings $W$). No new instrumentation is added; the mitigation uses data fusion from these existing measurements to implement a simple feedback correction to process parameters (back-off speed/hold pressure) that affects part weight and screw recovery consistency.
